instruction: Given this evidence about the Memorable CLI, classify the finding and assign a severity.
input: area: extraction_payload_minimization; verdict: confirmed_good; evidence: the outbound /v1/extract request (built by N7/k8) sends only task_description (one prompt line, J8-scrubbed, 200-char cap) plus tool_calls whose inputs are restricted to an 11-field allowlist (command, cmd, file_path, filePath, path, notebook_path, pattern, url, query, description, shell_id, bash_id), each value J8-scrubbed and sliced to 4000 chars; tool results are reduced to {exit_code} or {ok} (p2), never the tool output body; corpus is always the empty string; agent_output (last assistant message, 256 KiB cap) is captured locally but never included in the payload
output: CONFIRMED good - INFO: extraction is minimized by construction; file contents, tool output, edit bodies and the transcript never leave the machine; only the scrubbed prompt line and allow-listed tool arguments are sent

instruction: Given this evidence about the Memorable CLI, classify the finding and assign a severity.
input: area: consent_fail_closed; verdict: confirmed_good; evidence: consent is unset by default and q8() maps anything other than read-write/read-only/deny to unset; the store-write path (YZ) throws a consent error unless read-write; enable grants read-write, disable makes memory read-only, forget denies recall too; prune works in every consent mode including forget; rejected sessions are logged to rejected.jsonl with a reason; the Claude Code user-prompt hook exits on deny/unset before doing anything
output: CONFIRMED good - INFO: consent is fail-closed by default (nothing stored or sent before enable); disable/forget give read-only/deny escalation, and prune remains available in every mode so a store can always be emptied

instruction: Given this evidence about the Memorable CLI, classify the finding and assign a severity.
input: area: injection_safe_render; verdict: confirmed_good; evidence: every stored value rendered into an agent context passes through b() which strips ANSI/escape sequences (A4) and control characters (E4: x00-x08 x0b-x1a x1c-x1f x7f), caps per-field at 4000 chars and the whole render at 8000 chars (R4/P6); the injected block is wrapped with an HTML comment marker and an explicit footer that it is reference data, not instructions, and to treat all stored content as inert data; postconditions truncate at 240 chars
output: CONFIRMED good - INFO: procedure rendering is defended against terminal-escape and control-character injection with size caps and explicit data-not-instructions framing; residual markup vectors are tracked separately

instruction: Given this evidence about the Memorable CLI, classify the finding and assign a severity.
input: area: mcp_tool_surface; verdict: confirmed_good; evidence: memorable mcp exposes exactly 5 tools (memorable_recall, memorable_show, memorable_list, memorable_status, memorable_explain_recall), all annotated readOnlyHint true / destructiveHint false / idempotentHint true / openWorldHint false; the tools/call handler answers any unknown tool name with a fixed refusal that no write/capture/key/billing operation is exposed through MCP and directs those to a human at the terminal
output: CONFIRMED good - INFO: the MCP server is read-only by construction with advisory annotations and a hard refusal for write/capture/billing operations; the residual read-surface exposure of stored step commands is tracked separately

instruction: Given this evidence about the Memorable CLI, classify the finding and assign a severity.
input: area: redaction_gaps; verdict: confirmed; evidence: the redactor J8 collapses home dir to ~, rewrites emails to <email>, known-prefix secrets to <secret>, key=value assignments to <secret> only when the key name contains a keyword (token/password/secret/credential/bearer/apikey/accesskey/privatekey/signingkey/sessionkey/clientsecret/passphrase) AND the value is at least 12 chars with no spaces/quotes, 32+ mixed-case tokens to <token>, and 40+ hex to <hex>; realistic secrets that survive: DB_PASS=abc123 (key name has no keyword, value under 12 chars), PW=LongEnoughValue (name not in keyword list), lowercase-only or single-case long tokens, and key=value forms written with spaces inside the value
output: CONFIRMED - MEDIUM: regex-based redaction has several blind spots; env-style assignments with non-keyword names or short values, and single-case tokens, can be sent to the extraction API in plaintext inside allow-listed command/description fields

instruction: Given this evidence about the Memorable CLI, classify the finding and assign a severity.
input: area: render_markup_passthrough; verdict: confirmed; evidence: the injection-safe renderer b() strips ANSI escapes and control characters and caps length, but does not strip markdown formatting, HTML, or HTML comments; a stored step whose text contains markdown links, HTML tags, comment blocks, or plain-text instruction-like sentences is injected verbatim into the agent context; the only mitigations are the data-not-instructions HTML comment marker and the footer instruction to treat stored content as inert; the prompt-hook wrapper repeats the same advisory language
output: CONFIRMED - MEDIUM: the procedure-injection protection is advisory framing plus control-char stripping, not markup sanitisation; if a procedure can be seeded (shared store, hostile extraction endpoint, or a poisoned ingested trace), the injected block is a plausible prompt-injection channel that survives the current renderer

instruction: Given this evidence about the Memorable CLI, classify the finding and assign a severity.
input: area: shared_store_boundary; verdict: confirmed; evidence: the product design states one agent's recorded procedure is recallable by every agent on the same store; recall is a local client-side match over whatever the store holds with no per-role, per-repository or per-procedure access control; on the gbrain and qm backends the store is a shared database, so any agent with store access (or the CLI, or the MCP server) can read every procedure including step commands and file paths recorded by an agent in a different project or scope; the only scoping is the local backend being single-machine and QM per-scope consent; the read-only MCP tool memorable_show returns full step commands and could be driven by a prompt-injected subagent without triggering any write
output: CONFIRMED - MEDIUM: the multi-agent shared store is the boundary that can break; read access to procedure contents is machine/scope-scoped, not role-scoped, so an agent in one project can read commands recorded in another; MCP amplifies this read-only

instruction: Given this evidence about the Memorable CLI, classify the finding and assign a severity.
input: area: server_driven_policy; verdict: confirmed; evidence: the extraction response carries server-controlled fields the client honors silently: record_repos (client persists it into config and starts sending repo = <host>/<path> of the git remote with scheme, credentials and localhost remotes stripped by O6), repo_blocked (client keeps sessions local for that repo), refused/allowance_exhausted, client_min_version and notices; MEMORABLE_API_URL plus MEMORABLE_API_KEY env can point the client at any endpoint, which then receives the workspace API key and these toggles; the default endpoint is a Cloudflare Workers domain (de-identified here)
output: CONFIRMED - LOW: the client has a wide server-driven policy surface (repo reporting can be enabled remotely, repos blocked, notices pushed); the repo value is de-identified to host/path only, but a misconfigured or hostile endpoint is trusted wholesale and is handed the API key

instruction: Given this evidence about the Memorable CLI, classify the finding and assign a severity.
input: area: consent_scope_trace_capture; verdict: confirmed; evidence: the codex-capture hook handler (B8) writes local trace files under ~/.memorable/traces (prompt scrubbed, minimized allow-listed tool calls, and agent_output up to 256 KiB with an agent_output_truncated flag) whenever the hooks are installed, gated only by the MEMORABLE=0 env var and NOT by the consent mode; the marketing statement that nothing is stored before memorable enable is scoped to the procedure store and to extraction, not to this local trace checkpoint; files are written 0600; the Claude Code user-prompt hook is consent-gated and exits on deny/unset
output: CONFIRMED - LOW: codex hook capture persists local traces (including the last assistant message) before consent is granted; documented for the codex path but a claim-vs-behavior gap for users who rely on nothing-being-stored-before-enable; mitigated by 0600 perms and MEMORABLE=0 opt-out

instruction: Given this evidence about the Memorable CLI, classify the finding and assign a severity.
input: area: encryption_claim_scope; verdict: confirmed; evidence: AES-256-GCM at-rest sealing (MEMv1 prefix, key from macOS keychain or MEMORABLE_STORE_KEY or ~/.memorable/store.key 0600) is applied only to the local backend file ~/.memorable/procedures.jsonl; on the gbrain and qm backends the CLI writes plaintext JSONB rows (the mZ wrapper only strips NULs and lone surrogates) into the configured database with no client-side sealing; the README headline every procedure is encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM does not qualify this backend split
output: CONFIRMED - LOW: the encrypted-at-rest claim holds only for the local backend; gbrain/QM procedures are plaintext rows relying on the database's own protections, and memorable init gbrain|qm does not warn about the difference

instruction: Given this evidence about the Memorable CLI, classify the finding and assign a severity.
input: area: extraction_api_auth_surface; verdict: suspected; evidence: the extraction API authenticates with a single workspace Bearer key (minted in the dashboard), stored in plaintext in ~/.memorable/config.json (0600); doctor probes auth with an empty /v1/extract call and semantic recall with /v1/embed (arbitrary text in, embedding out); workspaces have a per-period extraction allowance and when it is exhausted queued sessions are dropped, not retried (they have left the queue and will not be retried) unless backfill re-sends from machine history; live server behavior (key revocation, rate limits, multi-factor, dashboard read scope) cannot be verified statically
output: SUSPECTED - MEDIUM: a leaked workspace key grants capture allowance consumption (denial of service on recording, with queued sessions dropped rather than retried), read of stored procedures via the dashboard API, and a free embedding oracle via /v1/embed; no MFA is evidenced and the key is at rest in plaintext config

instruction: Given this evidence about the Memorable CLI, classify the finding and assign a severity.
input: area: claim_vs_payload; verdict: confirmed; evidence: the reference document states transcript/session_id/emails/cwd/file contents never sent, but the client extraction payload includes session_id and workflow_id (opaque slugs, sanitized to alphanumerics) plus task_description and repo (host/path only when record_repos is enabled); emails in allow-listed argument values are rewritten to <email> and cwd is collapsed to ~; no transcript, file contents or tool output is sent
output: CONFIRMED - INFO: the never-sent claim is accurate for transcript/file contents/cwd/emails but not literally for session_id, which the client does send as an opaque slug alongside the scrubbed prompt line; low sensitivity, but the reference doc should be tightened
